prompt: Gentle, slow movement therapy for seniors at home, NOT martial arts. The same woman, same studio, same clothes and lighting. She moves slowly and smoothly from the pose in the first frame to exactly the pose in the last frame, in one continuous motion, nothing else. She slides the left foot one small step forward (half a foot length); the stance stays short and tall, the front knee bends only slightly above the front foot, both heels end on the floor. The left forearm floats up above the forehead, palm turning outward, while the right palm pushes slowly forward at chest height. The torso turns slightly left. Tall, no lunge. She stays TALL the whole time: her hips remain high, her knees are only softly unlocked (a slight bend of a few degrees, never a squat, never a lunge, never a deep stance), each knee stays above its own foot, the back heels stay on the floor, the spine is vertical, shoulders relaxed, chin level, calm gentle face, natural breathing. Static locked camera, no camera movement, no zoom, no cuts, full body always in frame from head to feet, feet visible on the floor, background unchanged.
